title: Offer design: fix the offer before the copy, using the value equation and six-part anatomy
summary: Corey's offers skill argues the offer itself, not the sales page, is the main conversion lever. It gives a value equation to diagnose which lever is broken, a six-component offer anatomy, a diagnostic loop for stuck offers, and guardrails against fake scarcity, bonus inflation, and discounting to acquire.

principles.text: Improve the offer itself; better copy on a weak offer compounds slowly.
principles.quote: **The offer is the thing, not the page.** Better copy on a weak offer compounds slowly. A stronger offer with average copy converts immediately.

principles.text: Diagnose offers with the value equation: dream outcome and likelihood over time delay and effort.
principles.quote: most "lower the price" requests are actually "raise the numerator or lower the denominator" requests. Price is the comparison, not the value.

principles.text: A complete offer has six parts: deliverable, bonuses, guarantee, scarcity, name, price and payment structure.
principles.quote: A complete offer has six components. Skip any one and conversion suffers.

principles.text: Fix one lever per iteration, starting with the lowest-scoring one.
principles.quote: Pick one lever to fix this iteration — don't rebuild everything. The biggest lever is usually the one currently scoring lowest.

principles.text: Project lift honestly: multiply component lifts, and expect 10-40% from one change.
principles.quote: Two iterations rarely reach 2–3x; anyone promising 5x is selling something.

principles.text: Never discount to acquire new customers; reserve discounts for upgrades or real seasonal windows.
principles.quote: discount-*askers* churn at ~2× the rate of full-price customers, and a coupon anchors the product as cheap.
